summary: Gov. Kim Reynolds (Republican) did not run again, so the seat was open. Rob Sand (Democrat) won, defeating Zach Lahn (Republican).

candidates.name: Rob Sand
candidates.bio: Rob Sand is Iowa's state auditor, first elected in 2018 and reelected in 2022. His running mate was Dave Muhlbauer.

positions.summary: Says his cancer plan includes radon testing and water quality monitors, and has described a water quality crisis in Iowa.
Says he would reverse Iowa's Medicaid privatization through an executive order.
Says he would create universal all-day pre-K, paid for by ending state funding for private school vouchers.
Describes a remote-work program, "Statewide Work, Statewide Jobs," meant to help revitalize small towns and rural communities that have seen jobs and opportunities disappear.

candidates.name: Zach Lahn
candidates.bio: Zach Lahn is a businessman who won the Republican nomination in a June 2026 primary, beating U.S. Rep. Randy Feenstra. His running mate was Derek Wulf.

positions.summary: Says he would end state benefits for illegal immigrants.
Says he supports school choice, homeschooling and education savings accounts.
Says he would lower the property tax burden, expand paths to homeownership, and ban hedge funds from buying single-family homes.
Lists protecting life before birth among his Iowa First policies.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called). 2026-11-25: shares are computed from the totals KCCI reports (https://www.kcci.com/article/iowa-certifies-november-election-results-with-higher-voter-turnout/74522089), with the 1,756 write-ins The Green Papers shows in the total. Not marked certified: the Secretary of State release (https://www.rcreader.com/news-releases/iowa-state-board-canvassers-certifies-2026-midterm-election-results) says the Iowa Legislature certifies the governor race on the first day of its 2027 session.
